source_claims.statement: Code analysis found fillWithURI(). Preview endpoint icon parameter returned NULL. MIME type validation blocked content inspection.
After auth and MIME barriers, used SVG with type=image/svg+xml#.svg exploiting PHP extension extraction after #. Confirmed with sheriff server.

research_questions.formulation: After initial SSRF attempts return NULL due to MIME checks, can a crafted extension or fragment bypass the validation while still triggering the URI fetch?
research_questions.anchor: shift to SVG + # fragment after MIME barrier
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether MIME validation can be satisfied while controlling the fetched URL
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that MIME type checks fully close the SSRF

environment_model_updates: PHP extracts extension after # incorrectly for validation

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: code review of URL handling and auth flows
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: trying fragment and SVG type combinations after NULL responses

unobserved_history: exact sequence of MIME bypass attempts before SVG
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat NULL as proof of no SSRF
The bypass exploited a mismatch between validation and actual fetch
next_evidence_actions: Group with SRC-000019; note CVE-2024-52598 and fix in v5.4.1
layer_b_candidate_principles: When an SSRF is gated by MIME or content-type checks, test mismatches between how the extension is extracted for validation versus how the full URL is fetched
Fragment identifiers or type parameters can sometimes satisfy validators without changing the requested resource
model_vs_harness: Recognizing the PHP extension-extraction quirk is model reasoning; OOB confirmation and systematic auth/URI testing can be harness.
